input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: Section 20 meets the preferred position in full. Vendor gives an unqualified IP infringement indemnity covering the Services and Deliverables in favour of Customer, its Affiliates and their personnel (20.1), plus indemnities for Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (20.2). Standard procedure applies with a materiality-of-prejudice qualifier on notice and a settlement-consent protection (20.4), and Vendor bears the usual procure/modify/replace/refund remedies with no right to terminate unaffected Services (20.5). Customer's reciprocal indemnity is appropriately narrow, limited to unmodified Customer-supplied material used as authorised and Customer's own violation of Applicable Law, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications and Vendor instructions (20.3). Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under Section 21.3, so Vendor's indemnity sits outside the liability cap rather than being subject to any super-cap. No redline required.
